title: Recursive Reasoning or Statistical Extrapolation? In-Context Learning in Multi-Agent Interdependent Decision-Making
abstract: arXiv:2609.18591v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables large language model (LLM) agents to improve decisions using interaction history, yet it remains unclear whether such improvement reflects refined internal reasoning or mere extrapolation of statistical patterns. To disentangle these mechanisms, we study LLM agents in multi-agent incomplete-information games that require recursive belief reasoning. By constructing a public goods game and manipulating the statistical structure of historical feedback, we evaluate decision quality against a history-independent rational expectations equilibrium (REE) benchmark. Our experiments reveal that when historical statistical patterns are disrupted, the benefits of longer context largely vanish, degrading decision quality to the no-context baseline in a way sharply amplified by stronger strategic interdependence. These results suggest that, in such strategic environments, ICL behavior is more consistent with statistic

translated_title: 递归推理还是统计外推？多智能体相互依赖决策中的上下文学习
translated_abstract: 上下文学习使大型语言模型智能体能够利用交互历史来改进决策，但这种改进究竟反映了精细化的内部推理，还是仅仅是对统计模式的外推，目前仍不清楚。为了厘清这些机制，我们研究了多智能体不完全信息博弈中需要进行递归信念推理的LLM智能体。通过构建公共物品博弈并操纵历史反馈的统计结构，我们以独立于历史的理性预期均衡（REE）为基准来评估决策质量。我们的实验发现，当历史统计模式被打乱时，更长上下文带来的收益基本消失，决策质量退化到无上下文的基线水平，且这种退化在更强的策略相互依赖条件下被急剧放大。这些结果表明，在此类策略环境中，ICL行为更符合统计外推的特征。
tldr: 研究发现LLM智能体在多智能体相互依赖决策中的上下文学习主要依赖对历史统计模式的外推而非真正的递归推理，一旦统计模式被破坏，长上下文带来的决策优势便大幅消失。
en_tdlr: LLM agents' in-context learning in multi-agent interdependent decision-making primarily reflects statistical extrapolation of historical patterns rather than genuine recursive reasoning, as disrupting the statistical structure largely eliminates the benefits of longer context.
